blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines on Saturday acknowledged that crises in the Middle East, natural disasters and uncertainties surrounding multilateralism had tested its leadership of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) this year. Foreign Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro said the challenges forced the country to navigate shifting regional and global conditions while pursuing its priorities on maritime security, regional stability and cooperation. “Despite these achievements, the Philippines’ chairmanship was not without its challenges,” Lazaro said during the opening statement of the Asean Foreign Ministers’ Meeting (AMM) under the Philippine chairmanship.
